answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes each agent stake funds before joining: like a ship paying to dock at a wharf, the stake is locked and slashed if the agent misbehaves. A newcomer with no history stands on a narrow ledge, one bad act forfeits the deposit. This is no fable: an attacker who wants a hundred fake identities must fund a hundred deposits, so creating Sybils costs real money instead of being free.
